media.alt_text:
Wood packing material checklist. Use the questions below to check wood packaging material (WPM) compliance before shipment to the United States.

IPPC ISPM-15 marking: Are all WPM stamped with International Plant Protection Convention IPSM-15 marks that are easily visible?

Stamping compliance: Are all stamps in compliance with ISPM-15 format?

Material Consistency: Is all the same wood used throughout? If not, are the different parts compliant?

Debarked: Is all bark removed from the WPM?

No live pests: Are there borer holes, tunnels, or loose or compacted sawdust in or on the WPM? This could indicate the presence of live pests.

media.alt_text:
Biological materials checklist. Use the questions below to assist with importing biological materials into the United States.

Gather documents: Do you have the required paperwork for the material, such as invoices or permits from regulating partner government agencies?

Package and label: Have you confirmed if the material is packaged and labeled according to transportation regulations, especially if it is a hazardous item?

Declare or Manifest: Did you satisfy CBP declaration or manifest requirements for the material, either orally or in writing?

File Entry: Have you confirmed if the material requires an entry filing, such as commercial goods exceeding $2,500 in value? 

Schedule inspection: Did you know all imported materials are subject to inspection? Use the CBP One mobile app to make an appointment at participating airports.
